mainTopic: רבי מאיר's concern for a minority, why only the girls of the כותים are נדות from the cradle, and the דרשה of "וְאִשָּׁה" for young girls
overview: The גמרא shows that רבי מאיר is the תנא who worries about a small minority. In a ברייתא he forbids minors from doing יבום, in case the boy turns out to be a סריס or the girl an אילונית, while the חכמים simply follow the majority. The גמרא objects that this may only be a common minority. It answers that baby girls seeing blood is also common, citing three incidents where a baby girl was immersed before her mother. A side question asks why the baby in פומבדיתא needed טבילה outside ארץ ישראל. מר זוטרא answers that it was so she could be smeared with תרומה oil, since smearing counts like drinking. The גמרא then explains that only the girls of the כותים were made נדות from the cradle, because we learn from "וְאִשָּׁה" to separate even a baby girl who sees blood, and they do not. Two ברייתות seem to use "וְאִשָּׁה" for different ages. רבא answers that these are traditions only leaned on verses. The amud ends by asking why a verse is needed for a law that is a tradition; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: It is רבי מאיר: minors do neither חליצה nor יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the view which worries about a minority is רבי מאיר's. It brings a ברייתא where he rules that a minor boy or girl can do neither חליצה nor יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי מאיר, as a ברייתא teaches: a minor boy and a minor girl do not do חליצה and do not do יבום. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it just asked: which תנא worries about a small minority? It says it is רבי מאיר, and quotes a ברייתא to show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling itself does not yet show any worry about a minority. The reason only comes out in the next steps, when the חכמים question him and he explains. So this step gives the source, and the coming back-and-forth shows why it proves the point.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor boy or girl, someone who has not yet reached adulthood
The ceremony that frees a childless widow from her tie to her husband's brother
Levirate marriage: the brother marries the childless widow of his deceased brother
A small minority; the question is who worries about it

steps.confusionAlert: The ruling covers both sides. A minor boy whose brother died cannot do חליצה or יבום with the widow. A minor girl whose husband died cannot do חליצה or יבום with her husband's brother.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Meir, as it is taught:
A minor boy and a minor girl
do not perform chalitza and do not perform yibum,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question of which תנא worries about a minority
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The view is רבי מאיר's, as seen in his ruling that minors do neither חליצה nor יבום
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר worries about a minority
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about minors and חליצה/יבום
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטן and a קטנה do not do חליצה or יבום

steps.title: The חכמים accept the חליצה part but ask about יבום
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים agree that minors can't do חליצה, because the פסוק says 'man' and a woman is compared to a man. They ask why minors can't do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי מאיר: You said well that they do not do חליצה, since 'man' is written in the section, and we compare a woman to a man. But what is the reason they do not do יבום?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים agree with half of רבי מאיר's ruling and challenge the other half. They want to know his reason for forbidding יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חליצה there is a clear source: the פסוק says 'man', so a minor boy is excluded. Through a הקש, the woman is compared to the man, so a minor girl is excluded too. For יבום there is no such word, so the חכמים ask what his reason is.

keyTerms.meaning: You said well, meaning we agree with this part
'Man', the word in the פסוק that excludes a minor
We compare (by הֶקֵּשׁ), giving one case the same law as another
The section of the תורה, here the section on חליצה

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Meir:
You said well that they do not perform chalitza,
since "man" is written in the passage,
and we compare a woman to a man.
But what is the reason they do not perform yibum?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר: יָפֶה אָמַרְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the יבום half of רבי מאיר's ruling in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that minors may not do יבום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'man' only appears in the חליצה section, so there is no clear source that excludes minors from יבום

steps.title: רבי מאיר's reason: the child may turn out to be a סריס or אילונית
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר explains that a minor might later prove unable to have children. Then the יבום would have been a forbidden relationship with no מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: A minor boy, in case he turns out to be a סריס. A minor girl, in case she turns out to be an אילונית. Then they would be involved in a forbidden relationship where there is no מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר answers the חכמים. He forbids יבום because the child might grow up unable to have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother's wife is normally an ערוה (a forbidden relationship). יבום permits her only because of the מצוה. If the boy turns out to be a סריס or the girl an אילונית, there was never a מצוה here, so the marriage was forbidden. רבי מאיר worries about this even though such cases are a minority.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who never develops physically and cannot have children
A woman who never develops physically and cannot have children
A forbidden relationship
Where there is no מצוה that would permit it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is exactly what the גמרא needed: רבי מאיר acts on a fear about something uncommon, which shows he worries about a minority.

phrases.english: He said to them:
A minor boy, lest he be found to be a saris,
a minor girl, lest she be found to be an aylonis,
and they will turn out to be engaging in a forbidden relationship
where there is no מצוה.
phrases.notes: A brother's wife is only permitted for the sake of the מצוה of יבום. Without the מצוה, she stays forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: קָטָן — שֶׁמָּא יִמָּצֵא סָרִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' question from step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason based on worry about a possible future discovery
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a word like 'man' in the פסוק, there seemed to be no reason to bar minors from יבום
steps.terutzMaskana: Minors are barred from יבום for fear they will turn out to be a סריס or אילונית, which would make the union a forbidden ערוה

steps.title: The חכמים follow the majority: most children are not like that
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the חכמים follow the majority. Most boys are not סריסים and most girls are not אילוניות, so they are not worried. This shows that רבי מאיר is the one who worries about the minority.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים? Follow the majority of minor boys, and most minor boys are not סריסים. Follow the majority of minor girls, and most minor girls are not אילוניות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the חכמים deal with רבי מאיר's worry. It answers that they simply go by the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that a סריס or אילונית cannot do יבום. They disagree only about whether to worry about the rare chance. The חכמים rely on רובא, while רבי מאיר worries about the מיעוטא. That is why רבי מאיר is the תנא the גמרא was looking for.

keyTerms.meaning: Go after the majority; decide by what is usually true
Majority
They are not ...

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר worries about a small minority (חייש למיעוטא), so he forbids minors from doing יבום. The חכמים follow the majority (רובא), and most children turn out fine.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
Go after the majority of minor boys,
and most minor boys are not sarisim;
go after the majority of minor girls,
and most minor girls are not aylonios.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר's reason in step 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the חכמים respond to רבי מאיר's worry about a סריס or אילונית
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They follow the majority, and most minors are not like that
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר worries about a minority while the חכמים follow the majority, which confirms that רבי מאיר is the תנא who is חייש למיעוטא

steps.title: Maybe רבי מאיר only worries about a common minority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: we only know that רבי מאיר worries about a common minority, like a סריס or an אילונית. We never heard that he worries about a rare minority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, you heard that רבי מאיר worries about a minority that is common. But a minority that is not common, did you ever hear him worry about that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 4. Maybe רבי מאיר only worries about minorities that come up often.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed that רבי מאיר worries about the minority of boys who turn out to be סריסים and girls who turn out to be אילוניות. Those cases are fairly common. Our case, a very young girl who sees blood, may be rare, so the proof may not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: A common minority, something that does not happen most of the time but still happens often
An uncommon minority, a rare case
Say / you can say, here used as 'granted, you can say that…'

phrases.english: Say that you heard that Rabbi Meir
is concerned for a common minority,
phrases.notes: He means the minority from Step 4: boys who turn out to be סריסים and girls who turn out to be אילוניות.

phrases.english: but an uncommon minority —
did you hear him say that?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מִיעוּטָא דִּשְׁכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof in Step 4 that רבי מאיר is the one who worries about a minority.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that רבי מאיר's concern for a minority applies to our case of a young girl seeing blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Concern for a common minority does not prove concern for a rare minority.

steps.title: Baby girls seeing blood is also a common minority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this minority is also common. It proves this from three separate incidents, reported by רבי יוסי, רבי, and רב יוסף, where a baby girl was immersed before her mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also a common minority. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי said there was a case in עין בול where they immersed a baby girl before her mother. רבי said there was a case in בית שערים where they immersed a baby girl before her mother. And the גמרא adds that רב יוסף, a later אמורא, said there was a case in פומבדיתא where they immersed a baby girl before her mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the objection and says baby girls seeing blood is not so rare. It brings three real stories from three different places to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Immersed before her mother' means the newborn saw blood so soon that she needed טבילה before her mother finished her own time after giving birth. Since this happened in three different places, it counts as a common minority. So רבי מאיר would worry about it too.

keyTerms.meaning: This one too
An incident, a real case that happened
They immersed her in a מקוה
Before her mother

steps.whatToRemember: Three separate incidents show that a newborn girl seeing blood is a common minority, not a rare one.

phrases.english: This too is a common minority.
As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei said:
There was an incident in Ein Bul
and they immersed her before her mother,
And Rabbi said: There was an incident in Beit She'arim
and they immersed her before her mother.
And Rav Yosef said: There was an incident in Pumbedita
and they immersed her before her mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise: the minority in question is in fact common.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Baby girls seeing blood is a rare minority, so רבי מאיר would ignore it.
steps.terutzMaskana: It happened in several places, so it is a common minority that רבי מאיר does worry about.

steps.title: Why did the baby in פומבדיתא need immersion at all?
steps.stepSummary: The incidents in ארץ ישראל make sense because of תרומה there. But in פומבדיתא, outside ארץ ישראל, שמואל says only eating תרומה is forbidden to such a person, not touching it. So why immerse the baby?
steps.simpleTranslation: The cases of רבי יוסי and רבי make sense, because of the תרומה of ארץ ישראל. But why did רב יוסף's case need it? Didn't שמואל say: the תרומה of outside ארץ ישראל is forbidden only to someone whose טומאה comes out of his own body, and that is only for eating, not for touching!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a side question about the third incident. Why would a baby girl in בבל need טבילה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ארץ ישראל, a girl who is a נדה would make תרומה impure by touching it, so she needs טבילה. Outside ארץ ישראל, שמואל rules that such a person is only forbidden to eat תרומה, not to touch it. A baby does not eat תרומה, so רב יוסף's case seems to have no reason for the טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part makes sense
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which must be kept טהור
תרומה separated outside ארץ ישראל, which has a lighter status
Impurity that comes out of one's own body, like a נדה or a זב
Eating
Touching

steps.confusionAlert: This question does not attack the main proof. It only asks why the טבילה was needed in בבל. The point that baby girls seeing blood is common still stands.

phrases.english: Granted, the cases of Rabbi Yosei and of Rabbi —
they were because of the teruma of Eretz Yisrael,
but why do I need Rav Yosef's case?
But didn't Shmuel say:
Teruma of outside the Land is forbidden
only to one whose impurity comes out of his body,
and that applies only to eating,
but not to touching!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וּדְרַבִּי מִשּׁוּם תְּרוּמַת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a side difficulty about the third incident brought in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's incident in פומבדיתא, where the baby was immersed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל rules that outside ארץ ישראל, a person with bodily טומאה is only forbidden to eat תרומה, not to touch it. So there is no reason to immerse a baby there.

steps.title: The immersion was so she could be smeared with תרומה oil
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא answers that the טבילה was needed so the baby could be smeared with oil of תרומה. A ברייתא learns from a פסוק that smearing and drinking count like eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: It was needed only for smearing her with oil of תרומה. As a ברייתא teaches: 'And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel, which they set apart for ה׳'. This comes to include one who smears and one who drinks.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא answers the question of Step 7. The baby needed טבילה so she could be rubbed with תרומה oil, which counts like eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל forbids only eating, not touching, outside ארץ ישראל. But the ברייתא teaches from a פסוק that smearing oil counts like eating. So a baby who would be rubbed with תרומה oil needs טבילה even in פומבדיתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for… (pointing to the specific case where the rule matters)
Smearing or rubbing oil on the body
To include, the פסוק adds more cases
One who smears oil
One who drinks

steps.whatToRemember: Smearing oil of תרומה counts like eating it, so even outside ארץ ישראל a baby girl who saw blood needs טבילה before being smeared with it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the general rule that סיכה is treated like eating, which keeps all three incidents meaningful as proof that the minority is common.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְסוּכָהּ שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: It was needed only to smear her with oil of teruma,
phrases.notes: Smearing counts like eating, and eating is forbidden even outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: ״וְלֹא יְחַלְּלוּ אֶת קׇדְשֵׁי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: As it is taught: "And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel
which they set apart for the Lord" —
to include one who smears and one who drinks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְסוּכָהּ שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a specific case where the rule still applies: smearing, which counts like eating.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Outside ארץ ישראל a baby girl never needs טבילה, since she does not eat תרומה and touching is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: She needs טבילה so she can be smeared with תרומה oil, since smearing is treated like eating.

steps.title: Why do we need a פסוק for drinking?
steps.stepSummary: Continuing מר זוטרא's proof, the גמרא asks why a פסוק is needed to teach that drinking is forbidden, since drinking is already part of eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a פסוק for one who drinks? Drinking is already included in eating!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא, continuing מר זוטרא's proof, questions the ברייתא he just quoted. Why would the פסוק need to teach us about drinking at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that drinking falls under the category of eating. So a פסוק that adds drinking seems to teach nothing new. This question sets up the real lesson of the פסוק in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Drinking
Eating
Included in

phrases.english: Why do I need a verse for one who drinks?
Drinking is included in eating!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא that מר זוטרא quoted in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a פסוק to include drinking.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Drinking is already part of eating, so a separate source for drinking teaches nothing.

steps.title: The פסוק really adds smearing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא really means the פסוק teaches that smearing counts like drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק comes to include one who smears, that he is like one who drinks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by rereading the ברייתא. The פסוק is not really adding drinking; it teaches that smearing oil counts like drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since drinking does not need its own source, the extra wording must be teaching something new: smearing. This is exactly what מר זוטרא needed. A baby smeared with oil of תרומה is like one who eats it, so she had to be טהור first.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (to add something to the law)
One who smears or anoints with oil

steps.whyThisMatters: This proves מר זוטרא's answer: the טבילה in פומבדיתא was needed so the baby could be smeared with oil of תרומה.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to include one who smears as one who drinks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the purpose of the extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to teach only about drinking, which we already knew.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that smearing counts like drinking, and so like eating.

steps.title: A second פסוק that smearing is like drinking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another source: a פסוק in תהלים compares water going inside the body to oil going into the bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it from here: "And it came into his innards like water, and like oil into his bones."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different פסוק to prove the same point. It compares oil soaking into the bones to water going into the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts oil on the body side by side with water drunk inside the body. This shows that oil soaking in through the skin is treated like drinking. It is a second, separate way to reach the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer or source)
From here

phrases.english: And if you want, say it from here:
"And it came into his innards like water,
and like oil into his bones."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source for the rule from Step 10.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק in תהלים 109:18 that compares water inside the body to oil in the bones.

steps.title: Then our girls should also be נדות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if we worry about the minority of baby girls who see blood, our own Jewish girls should also be treated as נדות from the cradle.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, ours too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main topic. If רבי מאיר worries about this minority for the girls of the כותים, why not for our girls too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5-6 showed that a baby girl seeing blood is a common enough minority for רבי מאיר to worry about. If the reason is just this minority, it should apply to Jewish girls as well. Yet we do not treat every Jewish baby girl as a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Ours (our girls)

phrases.english: If so, ours too?
phrases.notes: He means: we should treat our own baby girls as נדות from the cradle too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of smearing and returns to רבי מאיר's worry about the minority.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only the girls of the כותים are נדות from the cradle.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason is a common minority of baby girls who see blood, that minority exists among Jewish girls too.

steps.title: We separate our girls; the כותים do not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: we learn from "וְאִשָּׁה" that a baby girl can be a נדה, so we separate our girls when they see blood. The כותים do not, so the חכמים made a גזירה on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We, who learn from "אשה" and "ואשה," separate our girls when they see blood, so the חכמים did not decree on them. They, who do not learn "אשה" and "ואשה," do not separate their girls when they see blood, so the חכמים decreed on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the difference between us and the כותים. We already treat a baby girl as a נדה when she sees blood, so no extra rule is needed for us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with the כותים is not only the minority itself. Since they do not know a baby girl can be a נדה, they ignore her blood completely. So the חכמים made a blanket rule that all their girls are נדות; for us there was no need.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn out (from a פסוק)
We separate (keep away as a נדה)
The חכמים made a decree (a גזירה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the גזירה of the משנה applies only to the girls of the כותים and not to Jewish girls.

phrases.english: We, who learn from "a woman" and "and a woman,"
and when they see blood, we separate them —
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets, "we separate," is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: the Sages did not decree about them.
They, who do not learn from "a woman" and "and a woman,"
phrases.notes: "They" are the כותים from the משנה.

phrases.english: and when their girls see blood, they do not separate them —
the Sages decreed about them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The minority of baby girls who see blood should make all girls, Jewish and כותים, נדות from the cradle.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the כותים need a גזירה, because they do not separate their girls when they see blood; we do.

steps.title: What is the דרשה of אשה and ואשה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the דרשה of "אשה" and "ואשה" is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is "a woman" and "and a woman"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the דרשה it just mentioned. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 relied on a דרשה without explaining it. Here the גמרא asks for the details, so we know where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: What is

phrases.english: What is "a woman" and "and a woman"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the דרשה used in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact source and meaning of the דרשה "אשה" and "ואשה."

steps.title: Even a one-day-old girl can be a נדה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that "אשה" alone means an adult woman, and the extra "ו" in "ואשה" adds even a one-day-old girl to the laws of נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: "A woman" — I only know about a woman. From where do I know that a one-day-old girl can be a נדה? The פסוק says: "And a woman."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to answer the question. The extra letter ו in "וְאִשָּׁה" teaches that even a one-day-old baby girl can become a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "אשה" by itself would mean only a grown woman. The added ו means "and," which comes to include more: even a baby girl. This is why we separate our own girls when they see blood.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (from the plain words)
A one-day-old baby girl
A woman who is טמא because she saw menstrual blood
The פסוק teaches (by saying)

steps.whatToRemember: We learn from "וְאִשָּׁה" that even a one-day-old girl can be a נדה. Since we separate our girls when they see blood, the חכמים made a גזירה only on the girls of the כותים, who do not.
steps.confusionAlert: The baby is not a נדה just because she is a baby. She becomes a נדה only if she actually sees blood; the גזירה on the כותים is a special extra rule.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: "A woman" —
I only know about a grown woman.

phrases.aramaic: תִּינוֹקֶת בַּת יוֹם אֶחָד לְנִדָּה מִנַּיִן?
phrases.english: From where do I know that a one-day-old girl can be a נדה?
The verse teaches: "And a woman."
phrases.notes: The extra ו, meaning "and," is what adds the baby girl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא learns from the extra ו in "וְאִשָּׁה" that even a one-day-old girl is included in the laws of נדה.

steps.title: The same extra letter is used for two different ages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא just quoted uses "וְאִשָּׁה" to include a one-day-old girl, while another ברייתא uses the same word to include a girl of three years and one day for ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems that when the verse includes young girls, it includes even a one-day-old. But here is a contradiction: another ברייתא says, "'A woman' teaches only about an adult woman. From where do we know that a girl of three years and one day counts for relations? The verse says 'And a woman'!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction between two ברייתות. Both learn from the same extra "ו" in "וְאִשָּׁה", but they reach different ages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 the extra "ו" of "וְאִשָּׁה" brought in even a one-day-old girl. Here a second ברייתא, on the nearby פסוק about ביאה, uses the same kind of extra "ו" to bring in only a girl from three years and one day. If the extra "ו" includes young girls, it should include them from the same age in both places.

keyTerms.meaning: "Apparently" or "so we see". It draws a conclusion from what was just said.
"And they set them against each other". It introduces a contradiction between two sources.
Marital relations
"The verse teaches". It introduces the פסוק used as the source.

steps.confusionAlert: Both ברייתות learn from the extra "ו" of "וְאִשָּׁה", in two neighboring פסוקים (ויקרא 15:19 for נדה, ויקרא 15:18 for ביאה). That is why the גמרא sees a clash: the same kind of extra "ו" gives two different minimum ages.

phrases.english: So we see that when the verse includes young girls,
it includes even a one-day-old girl.
But a contradiction is raised:
"A woman": from this I know only about an adult woman.

phrases.aramaic: תִּינוֹקֶת בַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: A girl who is three years and one day old,
from where do we know she counts for relations?
The verse says: "And a woman"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא, כִּי מְרַבֵּי קְרָא בַּת יוֹם אֶחָד מְרַבֵּי, וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of "וְאִשָּׁה" given in step 15 by setting a second ברייתא against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא in step 15, which uses "וְאִשָּׁה" to include a one-day-old girl.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא uses the same extra "ו" to include only a girl of three years and one day, so one letter seems to be giving two different starting ages.

steps.title: רבא: these laws are traditions only leaned on the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that these laws are really הלכות passed down by tradition, and the חכמים only attached them to verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: These are traditional laws, and the חכמים leaned them on verses.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the contradiction. He says the laws do not truly come from the extra "ו". They are traditions, and the verse is only a support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the laws were truly learned from "וְאִשָּׁה", one letter could not teach two ages. But if they are traditions that the חכמים only hooked onto the פסוק, the verse is not their real source, so there is no clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A law passed down by tradition, here meaning a הלכה למשה מסיני
"They leaned them". The חכמים attached the law to a verse as a support, not as its real source.
Verses (plural of קְרָא)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up an important idea: a law can be linked to a פסוק without the פסוק being its true source.

phrases.english: רבא said: They are traditional laws,
phrases.notes: He means laws given to משה at סיני and passed down orally.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis leaned them on verses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the source: the verse is only a support, and the law itself comes from tradition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both laws come from the extra "ו" in "וְאִשָּׁה", so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The laws are traditions that were only leaned on the verse, so there is no real contradiction.

steps.title: Which law is from the verse and which is from tradition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the two laws is really taught by the verse and which is the tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one comes from the verse, and which one is a tradition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבא's answer. This sets up the next two steps, where it tries out each option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer suggests that at least one of the two laws is a tradition. The גמרא now wants to know which law that is and which law still comes from the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: "Which one?"
A verse

phrases.english: Which one is from the verse, and which one is a tradition?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a more exact version of רבא's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the two laws (the one-day-old for נדה or the three-years-and-a-day for ביאה) is the tradition, and which comes from the verse?

steps.title: The first option fails because the verse sets no age
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the one-day-old law is the tradition and the three-year law is from the verse, because the verse sets no age limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose you say the one-day-old law is the tradition and the three-years-and-a-day law is from the verse. But the verse is written with no limit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out the first possible answer and pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "וְאִשָּׁה" do not mention any age. A verse with no age limit would naturally include girls from birth, not only from age three. So the verse cannot be the source of a law that starts at three years and one day.

keyTerms.meaning: "If you say". It introduces a suggestion that is about to be rejected.
General, unspecified, with no limit given

phrases.english: If you say the one-day-old law is the tradition,

phrases.aramaic: בַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד — קְרָא,
phrases.english: and the three-years-and-one-day law comes from the verse,
but the verse is written with no limit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the option that the three-year law comes from the verse.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: "וְאִשָּׁה" sets no age, so it cannot be the source of a law that begins specifically at three years and one day.

steps.title: The three-year law is the tradition; the one-day-old law is from the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles on the other option: the three-years-and-a-day law is a tradition, and the one-day-old law comes from the verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the three-years-and-one-day law is the tradition, and the one-day-old law comes from the verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer that works, which is the opposite of the option it just rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A verse with no age limit fits a law that starts from birth. So the verse teaches that a one-day-old girl can be a נדה, and the specific age of three years and one day for ביאה comes from tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather". It introduces the corrected answer.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד — הִלְכְתָא,
phrases.english: Rather, the three-years-and-one-day law is the tradition,
and the one-day-old law comes from the verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remaining option after step 19 rejected the first one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three-years-and-one-day law for ביאה is a tradition, and the law that a one-day-old girl can be a נדה comes from the verse.

steps.title: If it is a tradition, why do we need a verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the three-years-and-one-day law is a tradition, why does the ברייתא attach it to a verse at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: And since it is a tradition, why do I need a verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 20. Its reply comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A law from tradition stands on its own and does not need a פסוק. So why does the second ברייתא say "תלמוד לומר: ואשה" for the three-year law? The גמרא wants to know what the verse adds.

keyTerms.meaning: "Since"
"Why do I need it?" It asks what purpose something serves.

phrases.english: And since it is a tradition,
phrases.notes: He means the three-years-and-one-day law from step 20.

phrases.english: why do I need a verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of "וְאִשָּׁה" for the three-years-and-one-day law in the second ברייתא, now that this law is called a tradition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A law from tradition needs no verse, so linking it to "וְאִשָּׁה" seems to serve no purpose.
